title: Outflare
description: Requests, job queue, Postgres and process health for an Outflare server. See docs/monitoring.md in outflareai/outflare.

panels.title: Requests refused by rate limits
panels.description: 429s by limit: api (per token), register, site_ip (unknown site keys), site_key (per key), site_visitor (per visitor behind a site's proxy).

panels.title: Jobs due, by kind
panels.description: Jobs whose run_at has passed, waiting for a worker.

panels.title: Wait before a worker picks a job up (p95)
Jobs put back after their lease ran out
panels.description: Running jobs requeued because their worker stopped holding them (a crash, or a job longer than the lease). Each may run twice.

panels.title: Time waiting for a connection
panels.description: Above zero means the pool is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Below 99% means the working set no longer fits in memory.

panels.title: Sequential scans on large tables
panels.description: A large table scanned often is missing an index.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores in use.

panels.title: Oldest due item, by stage (the bottleneck)
panels.description: How long the longest-waiting item of each stage has waited for a worker. The highest line is the bottleneck: give that stage more workers, or find what it waits on below.

panels.title: Items due, by stage
panels.description: Items ready and waiting for a worker. A line that keeps growing is a stage that can't keep up.

panels.title: Items finished, by outcome
panels.description: What stages decided per second, across every worker.

panels.title: Why items stop
panels.description: Error and reason codes per second, by stage: rate limits, provider errors, AI failures, budget pauses, skips.

panels.title: Batch time (p95), by stage
panels.description: How long one batch takes. A slow stage with a small backlog is fine; a slow stage with a growing backlog needs more workers or a faster provider.

panels.title: Wait before a worker picks an item up (p95)
panels.description: Time from an item being due to being claimed, by stage.

panels.title: Calls held back by limits
panels.description: Calls to outside accounts that waited: rate is a rate limit, breaker is an account paused after repeated failures, probe is waiting for the one test call.

panels.title: Outside accounts: call outcomes and open breakers
panels.description: Calls by outcome per second, and accounts whose breaker is open now.

panels.title: Runs, by state
panels.description: Runs running or paused. Many paused runs usually means workspaces hit a budget or lost a connection.

panels.title: Items in progress and held
panels.description: Items claimed by workers, and items waiting for a person.

panels.title: AI calls by tool
panels.description: AI model calls booked per minute, by tool. Every call runs on the workspace's own key.

panels.title: AI spend by tool (US$ per hour)
panels.description: What AI calls cost on workspaces' own provider bills, by tool. Outflare pays for none of it.

panels.title: AI tokens by provider
panels.description: Tokens per minute, by provider and kind.

panels.title: AI limits warned and reached
panels.description: Workspaces told their AI spend reached 80% (level 80) or all (level 100) of a limit, per hour.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by outcome
panels.description: Deliveries connectors (such as Geonode) sent to /v1/hooks per minute. Normal is mostly accepted with a few duplicates; bad_signature or not_found in bulk means a wrong secret, an old address, or someone probing.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by connector
panels.description: Deliveries per minute by connector. A connector that drops to zero while it usually sends may have lost its subscription.

panels.title: Webhook events finished, by result
panels.description: Events workers finished per minute: handled, ignored (logged, nothing uses it yet), failed (gave up) and retry. Normal is no failed.

panels.title: Time from arrival to handled (p95)
panels.description: How long an event waits from arriving to a worker finishing it, by connector. Normal is a few seconds; minutes means workers are behind (see the Jobs row, kind hooks.handle).

panels.title: Domain Connect lookups by outcome
panels.description: Lookups per minute when a DNS card opens: available means the person can approve the records at their DNS provider. no_provider and not_onboarded are normal (the card falls back to a Cloudflare token); lookup_failed should stay near zero.

panels.title: Domain Connect lookup time (p95)
panels.description: How long a lookup takes, DNS and the provider's API included. Usually well under a second; cached answers are instant.

panels.title: Queries by outcome
panels.description: Queries run per minute, by outcome: invalid is SQL the database refused, timeout ran over 15 seconds, unavailable means the query role couldn't be set up.

panels.title: Query time
panels.description: How long queries take, at the median and the 95th percentile. Each runs on its own connection, at most 8 at once per server.
